items.text:
Running a Raspberry Pi or another SBC? OpenCreator for SBC runs the same stack there, with the printer's boards tunnelled over USB. Want to stay close to stock? OpenCreator Legacy works around FlashForge's software instead of replacing it.

Warranty and responsibility

OpenCreator's team and contributors take no responsibility for damage, wear or anything else that happens to your printer. If you brick or break it, that's on you, and installing mods may void your warranty. Be careful!

items.title: OpenCreator
items.text:
Open-source custom firmware for the FlashForge Creator 5 and Creator 5 Pro.

Kalico (Klipper) on the printer, a real toolchanger you control, AFC filament handling and Fluidd or Mainsail, all on the hardware you already own. Every part is open source and can be changed.

Get started Latest release Discord How we're different

items.title: Why OpenCreator?
items.text:
• Kalico on the printer

    A Klipper fork with MPC heater tuning, input shaper graphs drawn on the printer, power loss recovery and timelapse.

  • A real Klipper toolchanger

    Switch heads with T0–T3 with no extra software, load several tools in one go, and calibrate one nozzle without redoing all four. See how fast it changes

  • Filament that knows itself

    AFC with toolchanger support, ACE Pro auto feed and load, and material and colour synced into OrcaSlicer like an AMS.

  • Fluidd, Mainsail and GrumpyScreen

    Full web control, so the touchscreen is optional. A faster camera stream, SFTP, 3MF uploads and wired Ethernet with a USB adapter come with it.

  • Open and editable

    Plain Klipper configs, toggles for every behaviour and a plugin system. Every repository is on GitHub.

  • Active community

    Developers and Creator 5 owners in one place, for help, testing and what's next. Join the Discord

items.title: Pick your edition
items.text:
• OpenCreator CFW

    Replaces FlashForge's software with Kalico, Moonraker and a web UI on the printer's own computer. The full feature set.

  • OpenCreator for SBC

    The same stack on a Raspberry Pi or other SBC, for more speed and room than the printer's MIPS board.

  • OpenCreator Legacy

    Keeps the stock experience and adds comforts like a better camera. A slight change that really doesn't do much.

Development software

Don't treat any full custom firmware from us as complete. What you've seen from reviews, videos, or anything related outside of this wiki may be out of date, different, or not working.

Not sure which one? Is OpenCreator CFW for you? walks through what you gain and what you give up. The feature list and status and roadmap show what's finished and what's still in testing.

items.title: ACE Pro and ACE 2 Pro
items.text:
OpenCreator runs an Anycubic ACE Pro or ACE 2 Pro through AFC's own ACE unit (AFC_ACE for the ACE Pro, AFC_ACE2 for the ACE 2 Pro). On a Creator 5 each ACE slot feeds its own head: slot 1 feeds T0, slot 2 feeds T1, and so on. The heads' filament switches, about 450 mm before the gears, are where a feed stops.

Everything below lives in printer.ace.cfg next to printer.cfg. Change it in Fluidd or Mainsail and restart Klipper (FIRMWARE_RESTART) to apply.

Note

The ACE support described here is on the ace-upstream Kalico branch.

items.title: What happens with filament
items.text:
You do The printer does Put a new spool in a slot The ACE grips it, then feeds it all the way to that head's filament switch and stops. A spool put in during a print waits until the print ends. Press load (Fluidd, Mainsail or GrumpyScreen) The filament goes from the switch into the gears, the head heats to the filament's temperature and purges. Press unload The head heats first, the filament is pulled out of the head, and the ACE winds it back to just outside the unit. Press eject The ACE winds the filament fully back into the unit so you can take the spool out.

The load temperature comes from the spool: its Spoolman temperature if it has one, otherwise its material (default_material_temps in AFC/AFC.cfg, then a built-in table of about 50 filament types), otherwise the default there.

items.title: The unit
items.text:
[AFC_ACE2 ACE_1]          # [AFC_ACE ACE_1] for an ACE Pro
serial_port: auto
mode: direct
feed_speed: 100
retract_speed: 100
insert_feed_to_toolhead: True
Option Default What it does serial_port auto finds the ACE on USB, or give the device path. ace_index 1 Which ACE this is, when there is more than one. mode combined direct: each slot feeds its own head (the Creator 5 setup). combined: slots share a hub. feed_speed / retract_speed 100 Feed and wind-back speed in mm/s. insert_feed_to_toolhead False Feed a new spool to its head's switch on insert (on in the Creator 5 config). Off: it is only parked dist_hub out of the unit. insert_feed_step 10 The last part of that feed goes in steps of this many mm, checking the switch after each. insert_feed_extra 250 How far past the expected switch position it keeps stepping before giving up and winding back. load_approach_length / load_approach_speed 30 / 50 The last stretch before the switch goes this far at this slower speed. load_retry_pulse / load_retry_timeout 100 / 10 If the switch has not triggered after the feed, pulse this many mm for up to this many seconds. sensor_to_gears 0 After the switch, push this far on to the gears. 625 on a Creator 5. sensor_to_gears_speed 25 Speed for that push. sensor_to_gears_catch 0 The last this-many mm of it run with the extruder turning, so the gears catch the tip. 200 on a Creator 5. use_feed_assist True The ACE keeps feeding while the active head prints, so the extruder does not drag filament through the tube. assist_watchdog True Turns feed assist back on if it drops out during a print. stuck_spool_detection True (ACE 2) Pause when the spool stops turning while it should feed (a tangle). stuck_time 4 Seconds without spool movement before that counts as stuck. eject_buffer 475 Extra mm to wind back on eject, past dist_hub, to pull the filament fully into the unit. max_dryer_temperature 70 (ACE 2), 55 The highest dryer temperature AFC_ACE_DRY accepts. fallback_without_ace True With no ACE on USB, start without it (the heads work as their own lanes) instead of failing. missing_ace_wait 20 Seconds to wait for the ACE to appear after a boot before running without it. serial_log False Log every ACE message to AFC_ACE_serial.log. Only for debugging: it grows by about 10 MB every few hours.

items.title: The lanes, hubs and heads
items.text:
Each slot is a lane, with a hub (the tube to its head) and the head itself:

[AFC_lane lane1]
unit: ACE_1:1          # unit and slot
extruder: extruder0    # the head this slot feeds
hub: ACE_1_hub1
map: T0
dist_hub: 60           # mm from the slot to the park point just out of the unit

[AFC_hub ACE_1_hub1]
switch_pin: virtual
afc_bowden_length: 900          # park point to the head's switch
afc_unload_bowden_length: 900   # how far to wind back on unload

[AFC_extruder extruder0]
tool_stn: 70           # switch/gears to the nozzle on load
tool_stn_unload: 100   # how far the head pulls back on unload
tool_load_speed: 6
tool_unload_speed: 10

afc_bowden_length can be on the short side: the load pulses on until the switch triggers. To measure it, run AFC_ACE_CALIBRATE UNIT=ACE_1 LANE=lane1 with the head empty. It feeds until the switch triggers and saves the length.

items.title: Commands
items.text:
All take UNIT=ACE_1 (your unit's name).

Command What it does AFC_ACE_STATUS The unit's status and each slot's state. AFC_ACE_DRY TEMP=<C> DURATION=<minutes> [ROTATE=1] Start the dryer. ROTATE=1 turns the empty slots now and then. AFC_ACE_DRY_STOP Stop the dryer. AFC_ACE_TEMP_INFO Box, heater and room temperature and humidity. AFC_ACE_FAN SPEED=<0-100> The unit's fan (ACE 2). AFC_ACE_CALIBRATE LANE=<lane> Measure the park point to switch distance (afc_bowden_length). AFC_ACE_CALIBRATE_HUB LANE=<lane> Measure the slot to park point distance (dist_hub). AFC_ACE_LANE_RESET LANE=<lane> Wind a lane's filament back into the unit. AFC_ACE_STUCK_SPOOL_DETECTION ENABLE=0\|1 [STUCK_TIME=<s>] Turn tangle detection on or off until the next restart. AFC_ACE_SET_MATERIAL SLOT=<n> NAME=<text> Store a material name in a slot (ACE 2). AFC_ACE_BUFFER_STATE Each slot's buffer and filament sensors, for troubleshooting.

The normal AFC commands work too: TOOL_LOAD LANE=lane1, TOOL_UNLOAD, LANE_UNLOAD LANE=lane1 (eject), SET_MATERIAL, SET_COLOR.

items.title: The ACE's temperature and humidity
items.text:
Add the ACE's sensor to show it on the Fluidd or Mainsail dashboard:

[temperature_sensor ACE_1]
sensor_type: aht2x
afc_type: ACE2        # ACE for an ACE Pro
ace_unit: ACE_1
min_temp: 0
max_temp: 85

items.title: Running without the ACE
items.text: Unplug the ACE and restart Klipper: with fallback_without_ace: True the printer starts without it, and each head works as its own lane again (load by hand at the head). Plug it back in and restart Klipper to use it.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
The full custom firmware effort has layers (like an onion!) The printer's Linux host runs Klipper and web services. Four MCU boards perform motion, extrusion, heating, and sensing. AFC models the removable tools and filament state. Printer-side configuration ties those parts together.

Layer Current development role Source Linux host Runs Kalico (the Creator 5 Klipper fork), Moonraker, and the configured web interface. The printer is MIPS32 (Ingenic X2600 / Xburst 2 with 512MB of RAM) kalico Mainboard MCU Handles the main motion and machine I/O through the GD32 port. Chip is a gd32h737vgt6. Also uses a "MCLib" motion library for complex stuff like VFA compensation. See MCLib and motor control. kalico/src/c5_mainboardgd.c, c5_mclib.c and related target code, klippy/extras/mclib.py eboard MCU Drives the shared physical extruder motor and supplies the pressure-advance measurement interface. Chip is n32g455ccl7. kalico/src/c5_eboard.c, c5_eboard_pa.c and klippy/extras/pa_adjust.py Heaterboard MCU Handles tool heater and temperature I/O. Chip is n32g455rel7. kalico/src/stm32 N32G45x support (C5_HEATERBOARD build option) Levelboard MCU Supplies probe and levelboard-specific sensing used by calibration. Chip is n32g430f8s7. kalico/src/c5_levelboard.c and Klippy levelboard code Toolchanger and AFC Uses physical dock and grab inputs for T0 to T3 selection. AFC standalone provides filament and tool mapping, while creator5_toolchanger.py owns the machine-specific motion and safety checks. kalico/klippy/extras Printer filesystem Holds the Creator 5 configuration, AFC configuration, scripts, and printer data layout. opencreator-fs

items.title: Printer-side layout
items.text:
The SoC configuration is organized below /usr/data/opencreator/klipper/configs on the printer. printer.base.cfg includes the Creator 5, probe, motor, filament, vibration, Misc, and AFC files. G-code storage is configured at /usr/data/gcodes. Stock-format calibration data remains under /usr/data/firmwareRes/config, including extruder.json, zoffset.json, and test.json.

The Creator 5 has no chamber heater, chamber fans or aux fan, so those are in printer.pro.cfg. They're only included on a Creator 5 Pro, through printer.model.cfg. On the printer, that file is written at every boot, from the model in the stock boot script (MACHINE= in /usr/prog/app_startup.sh). In tunnel mode, the Pi installer asks which printer it's connected to. On a Creator 5, M106/M107 P2 and P3 do nothing, and M191 says there's no chamber heater instead of failing.

The config layout is originally based on FlashForge's default config layout, just expanded with new macros, settings, and removals of useless settings. This does not mean our config is interchangable with stock firmware, and if you try, it will not work as a lot of settings are intertwined with our Kalico.

There is one physical extrusion motor. The four Klipper extruder contexts select the corresponding tool heaters and state; they are not four independent extrusion drives. A toolchange must agree with the dock and grab pins before the selected logical extruder becomes active.

The single motor driver is configured on the eBoard as identical [tmc2209 extruder] through [tmc2209 extruder3] sections, one for each logical extruder for CFW. See MCU development and verification for pin assignments.

items.title: MCLib and motor control
items.text: The X, Y and Z motors are not driven by stepper driver chips. The GD32 mainboard drives each motor's two windings directly from its timer channels, and shapes the current itself. On stock firmware that shaping is FlashForge/GigaDevice's closed-source MCLib motor control library, loaded as libmcu-bare.bin from /usr/prog. Kalico ships a clean-room replacement for it, written from observing what the stock library does; the G-code commands keep their MCLIB_* names so existing config works.

items.title: What MCLib replaces
items.text:
Klipper normally tells a stepper driver "one step" and the chip handles the rest. Here there is no driver chip between the MCU and the motor coils:

Driver-chip Klipper Creator 5 mainboard Steps Driver chip microsteps internally MCU generates the winding current waveforms Current limit Set by driver config Closed-loop, controlled by firmware Feedback Usually none Phase currents read back by ADC at 20 kHz Lost steps Invisible Detectable in ours: the angle error is measured continuously

So the step pins the config lists for X, Y and Z (PJ0–PJ11) are not real GPIO. c5_mainboardgd_gpio.c maps them to virtual pins: writing X_STEP calls c5_mclib_step(), which advances the motor's electrical angle by one microstep; X_DIR sets the direction; X_EN enables or disables the winding drive; and reading X_ENDSTOP (PJ3/PJ7) actually returns the MCLib stall flag for that axis. Klipper's normal motion planning, homing and endstop logic all work unchanged on top of this.

The extruder is not MCLib: it lives on the eBoard behind a TMC2209, as described in MCU development. Kalico's replacement only covers the three mainboard motors.

items.title: The control loop
items.text:
flowchart TD
  subgraph host["Klipper host"]
    A[step queue]
  end
  subgraph mcu["GD32 mainboard"]
    B[virtual step pin<br/>advances electrical angle] --> C[20 kHz control loop]
    D[ADC phase currents] --> C
    C --> E[PI controllers<br/>+ observer estimates angle]
    E --> F[PWM compare values]
    F --> G[3 motor half-bridges]
    G --> H[motor coils]
    H --> D
  end
  A -->|serial| B

At about 20 kHz, per motor:

  1. Two ADC channels read the winding currents (ia, ib). The samples arrive by DMA into non-cached memory; a 2000-sample average first establishes the zero-current offset of each channel.
  2. An observer (a current observer with high-frequency injection) estimates the motor's real electrical angle from the current history.
  3. The estimated angle and the commanded angle (from the step pin) are compared. The error drives current PI controllers in the rotating d/q reference frame; the outputs go through an inverse transform back to per-winding voltages.
  4. The voltages become PWM compare values for the motor's timer, which drives the half-bridges.

Between steps, interpolate moves the commanded angle smoothly (the step interpolation in Quieter motors). When steps stop arriving for a while the motor drops to hold_current on a ramp; the currents decay to zero when disabled.

X and Y switch to a high-speed mode above a step-rate threshold (roughly 510 mm/s of belt travel): the speed controller takes over from the current controllers and resonance compensation is not applied there.

items.title: Configuring it
items.text:
Each motor has a [mclib stepper_*] section next to its normal [stepper_*]. Kalico sends it to the mainboard at connect time:

[mclib stepper_x]
motor_rs: 1.7     # winding resistance, ohm
motor_ls: 0.0026  # winding inductance, H
motor_km: 0.1729  # torque / back-EMF constant
bus_voltage: 24.0
run_current: 1.8
hold_current: 1.5
interpolate: True

The motor parameters set the PI gains and the observer model, so they need to match the real motor (the BJ42D29-30V22/V23 values are in printer.base.cfg). Runtime commands: MCLIB_SET_CURRENT changes the currents, MCLIB_SET_STALL the stall threshold, and MCLIB_SET_RESONANCE_DAMP / MCLIB_APPLY_CALIBRATION drive the VFA compensation tables. Values found by calibration are saved back into these sections by SAVE_CONFIG.

items.title: Stall and slip detection
items.text:
Added by OpenCreator

Stock MCLib reports nothing; the observer's angle error is there for the control, but stock never watches it. This detection, and the guard below, are OpenCreator additions built on our replacement.

Because the observer measures the real angle, the mainboard can tell when the motor isn't where it commanded it to be:

  • Stall: filtered torque drops below stall_threshold while the motor is running (armed after 17 quarter-steps of motion, and off during hold transitions and slow motion). Reads as the axis "endstop" pin.
  • Slip: the angle error drifts by whole electrical cycles (one cycle = four full steps), counted with hysteresis while moving.

The optional [c5_motion_guard] polls these counters twice a second over a print, ignores homing and toolchange windows, and warns or pauses when an axis loses steps (C5_MOTION_STATUS shows them). It needs mainboard firmware with the mclib_query_status command.

items.title: Firmware and updates
items.text:
The replacement is the portable core in src/c5_mclib.c (no hardware registers, unit-tested in test/c5_mclib.c) plus the hardware layer in src/stm32/c5_mainboardgd.c that sets up the timers, ADCs and DMA. scripts/build_c5_update.py builds the four board firmwares into stock update packages, and validates that the mainboard build contains the config_mclib command family and none of the commands the stock library used (mclib_set_pid_params, mclib_identify_motor, ...), so a half-updated board fails the build instead of the printer.

CPU faults are caught by c5_mainboardgd_fault.c, which turns the motor PWM outputs off before reporting; an unhandled fault would otherwise leave the windings energised.

items.title: Interfaces
items.text: The printer configuration currently uses AFC standalone mode, not a BoxTurtle or AMS-like mechanism. Mainsail/Fluidd exposes virtual Misc switches for flow calibration and purge. GrumpyScreen work is separate from the core Klipper and filesystem repositories, and is mostly kept up to date and commited to mainline SimpleAF GrumpyScreen.

items.title: Hardware
items.text:
Other than the previously explained hardware for the MCU chips, the printer has some unexplained "maximum" limits for temperature

Hardware Default Max Actual Max Safe Max Nozzles 320c 350c 350c? Chamber Heater (Pro) 65c 80c 70c? Bed 120 130 125?

Safe Max temps are the maximium safe temperatures before you run into actual hardware limitations. Anything with a ? may mean untested.

Known hardware limitations

  • Above 70 degrees chamber temperature, the grill will deform
  • Above 320 degrees, the nozzle may start recording wildly off temperatures

items.title: Research and inspiration
items.text:
Work we learned from without using its code:

  • Prusa Research, phase stepping (blog post, help article, Prusa-Firmware-Buddy, GPLv3). Their finding that each stepper motor has its own ripple, and that a per-motor correction calibrated with the toolhead accelerometer on diagonal moves can cancel most of it, is the idea behind Quieter motors. Our version runs on the Creator 5's own motor control (MCLib) rather than Trinamic drivers, keeps Klipper's steps, and calibrates a correction per speed; see that page for how it differs.

items.title: There were both human and AI use.
OpenCreator CFW Full Feature Set
items.text:
Finished works on a printer   Semi-Finished partly done   Testing in testing or untested   Broken not working yet

Feature Implementation Description ZMax on Print End Finished Puts the bed to the very bottom of the build area, for easy grabbing, a suggestion from @josemyab Allow for near zero purge printing Finished You can turn off purge and flow calibration to have almost zero purge on start, a half suggestion from @josemyab Purge line toggle Testing The purge line in front of the print has its own purge_line switch (on by default), separate from the bucket purge; see How to toggle features. Chamber heats with the bed (Pro Only) Testing Print start turns the chamber heater on together with the bed, without waiting for it, using the chamber temperature from the slicer's filament settings. Allow for calibration of only one toolhead Finished You don't need to calibrate all offsets to update z-offset of a nozzle, for switching nozzles. Saved baby stepping per tool Testing Baby stepping Z during a print is saved to that tool's Z offset, so the next print starts from it. LIST_BABYSTEP shows each tool's value and CLEAR_BABYSTEP TOOL= resets one or all; see Baby stepping. Allow for configuration of nozzle calibration Finished If your nozzle doesn't fit the min mm for levelboard, you can set it higher. Filament runout and switchover support Untested Give a tool a backup in AFC ("Infinite Spool") and a runout switches to it by itself, with the run-out tool's Tx commands sent to the backup. With no backup, it pauses and asks: switch to another loaded tool, or load new filament. AFC Toolchanger Finished Allows for the use of AFC filament system, but with toolchangers. Should be fully functional except for "loaded" filament buttons. GrumpyScreen Toolchanger Support Semi-Finished GrumpyScreen now properly shows all extruders and currently in use extruder, but you cannot extrude yet. Stock Feature Parity Finished Should have feature parity. Every FlashForge firmware version Finished Installs on any FlashForge release, 1.7.8 up to the latest 2.0.0 (kernel 2.0.8), with no need to update or downgrade first. See Supported FlashForge firmware. Early boot and recovery stick Testing OpenCreator boots from a file FlashForge updates don't overwrite, so it still starts (with Wi-Fi and SSH) when app_startup.sh breaks, and a runRecovery.sh on a USB stick runs before anything else to fix a printer that won't boot. A FlashForge update or rollback still boots stock. Safer than stock, where a broken app_startup.sh means opening the printer; see Early boot and recovery stick. Full WebUI support Finished You can avoid using the touchscreen, and don't even need it in general. SFTP over SSH Finished Transfer and manage files over SSH using SFTP, unlike stock firmware, which requires SCP for file transfers. SSH login banner Testing Logging in over SSH shows the OpenCreator logo with the uptime, IP address, free space, installed plugins and printer model, and a coloured prompt that shows the current folder; see Login banner. Plugins Testing Add-ons with their own Klipper modules, macros, Moonraker components and background programs, installed with oc-plugin from a catalog of official and unofficial plugins or any git URL. Plugins say which printers they're made for, and their logs are kept in check; see Plugins. Automatic Fan control for Heated Chamber (Pro Only) Finished Removes user fan control, and makes it automatically turn on when the chamber is set to something. Make Camera Better / Faster Finished Uses pre-installed MJPEG streamer over stock camera control in the touchscreen executable, making it efficient and fast. Input shaper graphs Finished CALIBRATE_INPUT_SHAPER_GRAPH calibrates input shaper and draws Klipper's frequency response graph for each axis on the printer itself, no PC needed; see Input shaper graphs. Timelapse Finished Moonraker Timelapse records a frame per layer from the printer camera and renders the video when the print ends; see Timelapse. Installed by the OpenCreator Installer. VDS filament dryer (SoC) Finished Start, stop and pause FlashForge's two-chamber dryer from Fluidd or macros, with each chamber graphed as a temperature sensor; see Filament dryer. Allow to switch toolheads arbitraily Finished You can send commands T0-T3 or click the buttons to pick up the toolheads. Allow to load multiple toolheads simultaneously Finished You can send the load command for multiple tools, which changes them, loads, then docks. Allow for reading colour information and material information on Orca Finished OrcaSlicer syncs the filament list from the printer like an AMS: material and colour for every tool. Needs a current OrcaSlicer development build. ACE Pro auto feed and auto load Finished Each ACE slot feeds its own head. A new spool is fed to the head's filament sensor by itself, and pressing load takes it into the gears and purges. Feeds made during a print wait until it ends. ACE Pro multiplexing Planned Several ACE slots feeding one head, in the planning stages. Raspberry Pi Host support Finished Allowing to use a Raspberry Pi over the stock MIPS32 CPU, by tunneling the MCUs through the SoC through gadget mode USBs. Power Loss Recovery Finished Allows to resume a print from power loss or MCU errors. The resumed print keeps its bed mesh, layer count, print time and estimates. Until you resume or discard it, the bed is kept at the print's temperature so the part stays stuck down; discarding turns the heaters off. Kalico Support Finished On all installs, you install Kalico, a beefed up Klipper fork with features such as MPC tuning. Removal of FlashForge services Finished You can completely disable FlashForge's things, and make it like it never existed. Full Orcaslicer with Moonraker Agent. Filament sync Finished Syncs your filaments (material and colour) into OrcaSlicer. Needs a current OrcaSlicer development build; older releases had a bug that broke it. Turn off cooling fan when chamber heater is on Finished It will actively say in console that it has been turned off, making it where cold air won't mess with the heated chamber Bed warp stabilization (bed soak) Finished Optionally waits at bed temperature for a configurable number of minutes immediately before a fresh mesh, letting the plate finish warping/expanding so the mesh reflects its settled shape instead of its heat-up transient. Skipped when the bed target is below 45 °C. Chamber heat wait toggle Finished Controls whether M191 blocks until the chamber actually reaches target, or just sets the target and lets the print start heating in the background while early layers print (M141-like). Toggle with C5_MISC_CHAMBER_WAIT_ON / OFF. OpenCreator Updater Finished A dedicated Moonraker update_manager entry that merges the latest config template into your live printer_data/config without clobbering values you've customized (speeds, toggle defaults, etc), then pulls Klipper -- all from one "Update" click. Uses a real three-way merge, so a conflicting change is left for you to resolve by hand instead of guessed at or silently overwritten. SoC/LoopScript installs get an equivalent boot-time version, not yet verified on real hardware. First-time setup dialog In development After installing, Fluidd, Mainsail and the screen walk you through pressure advance calibration, purging, Clog Detection and bed heat soak, point out the calibrations worth running (VFA on the printer; offsets, input shaper and VFA on an SBC), then point you to the Discord. Input shaper and PID come from FlashForge's calibration, imported on a first install. Shown until finished once; C5_FIRST_SETUP shows it again. 3MF uploads Finished Upload a sliced .gcode.3mf from OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio straight to Fluidd or from the slicer; the first sliced plate is extracted with its thumbnail. SBC installs. OpenCreator Fluidd theme Finished An extra-dark Fluidd theme with the OpenCreator logo. Installed and updated with the config. Updater self-repair Untested repair.sh fixes "No git repo detected" in the update manager: starts git where it is missing, syncs to the official main branch, fixes moonraker.conf. Door open notification Finished With C5_MISC_DOOR_NOTIFY_ON (or the door_notify switch in Fans & Outputs), opening the top or front door during a print, or starting a print with one open, shows an error pop-up in Fluidd and Mainsail and beeps (unless quiet mode is on). Uncomment [notifier door_open] in moonraker.conf to also get it on your phone. C5_DOORS shows whether each door is open. Chamber fan follows the heater Finished The chamber heater fan turns off as soon as the chamber heater's target is cleared, instead of running until the chamber cools below 50 °C. Chamber heater fan full speed toggle (Pro Only) Finished The chamber heater fan normally slows to half speed once the chamber is near its target. Turn on chamber_heat_fan_full in Fans & Outputs (or C5_MISC_CHAMBER_HEAT_FAN_FULL_ON / OFF) to keep it at 90% whenever the chamber heater is on. The setting survives restarts. Wi-Fi beep fallback Finished (Pi-tunnel) If a board is pinned to 4 tunnel ports (no dedicated beep serial channel), C5_BUZZER can fall back to sending the beep request over the network to the tunnel bridge instead of silently going quiet. Opt-in via network_host in [creator5_remote_beeper]. Quieter motors Testing The mainboard follows the real move between steps and cancels each X/Y motor's own wobble, calibrated with RIPPLE_CALIBRATE. Up to 40–60% less toolhead vibration at printing speeds; see Quieter motors. Needs the phase-stepping mainboard firmware. Quieter board fans Finished The mainboard and power supply fans ramp with the board's temperature and the power supply's load instead of running at full speed whenever the printer is busy; see Mainboard and power supply fans. MCU temperatures Finished The mainboard and toolhead board chips' temperatures show in Fluidd and Mainsail; see MCU temperatures. Wired Ethernet Finished The printer only has Wi-Fi, but a USB Ethernet adapter (or Android USB tethering) gives it a wired connection, used instead of Wi-Fi while the cable is in; see Wired Ethernet. Motion guard Testing Skipped step and stall detection for X, Y and Z, off by default; see Motion guard. VDS Support Finished VDS Support is available, but untested as no one on the development team owns a VDS or plans on owning a VDS.

items.title: Making the configs yours
items.text: OpenCreator's configs are plain Klipper config files, and you're free to change them. Updates merge into them instead of overwriting them, so your changes stay. This page shows where they are, how updates treat your edits, and the easiest way to keep your own settings separate.

items.title: Where the configs are
items.text:
Printer (SoC)Tunneled (SBC)

/usr/data/opencreator/klipper/config

~/printer_data/config on the SBC.

Open them in the web UI: Configuration (the {…} icon) in Fluidd, or Machine in Mainsail. Edit a file there, then press Save & Restart so Klipper loads it. A Klipper restart is all it takes; you don't need to reboot.

items.title: What's in each file
items.text:
printer.cfg is the one Klipper reads. It includes the rest:

File What it holds printer.cfg The includes, the TMC settings and, at the bottom, the SAVE_CONFIG block with your calibration printer.base.cfg The printer itself: MCUs, steppers, heaters and fans. It includes most of the files below printer.creator5.cfg The toolchanger ([creator5_toolchanger]): dock positions, toolchange speeds, purge and calibration settings printer.misc.cfg The switches and their macros printer.macro.cfg Print start, print end and the other OpenCreator macros printer.filament.cfg The filament wheel (clog) sensors printer.probe.cfg, printer.mesh.cfg The probe and the bed mesh printer.vibration.cfg The accelerometer and input shaper printer.motor.cfg The tool lock motor printer.pro.cfg Creator 5 Pro only: chamber heater and fans printer.mpc.cfg Kalico MPC helpers printer.override.cfg Shared pins and sections other files need first AFC/AFC.cfg, printer.afc-standalone.cfg AFC, lanes and tools

The installer and the printer write a few files themselves: printer.model.cfg, printer.accessory.*.cfg and printer.ace*.cfg. c5_misc_variables.cfg holds the switch states and AFC/AFC.var.* AFC's state. Leave these alone.

items.title: How updates treat your changes
items.text:
Every file OpenCreator ships is a template. When an update brings a new version, the updater merges it into your copy:

  • Your edits stay, unless the update changed the very same lines.
  • Your calibration stays. The SAVE_CONFIG block (input shaper, PID, meshes, skew) is never merged, only carried along.
  • Same lines changed on both sides: your file is left exactly as it is, and the merged version, with <<<<<<< markers, is put next to it as <file>.conflict. See Resolving a conflict.

Files that aren't templates, like a file you create, are never touched by updates.

items.title: The easy way: your own config file
items.text:
Instead of editing the shipped files, put your changes in a file of your own. Klipper reads a section that appears twice as one, and the value it reads last wins, so a file included at the end overrides the shipped values without changing them. Updates then never conflict with your settings.

  1. Create my-printer.cfg in the config folder. Any name works that isn't one of OpenCreator's files.

  2. In printer.cfg, add one line under [include plugins/*.cfg], above the SAVE_CONFIG block:

    [include plugins/*.cfg]
[include my-printer.cfg]

  3. Put the options you want to change in my-printer.cfg, under their section name, and restart Klipper.

Only the options you list change; everything else keeps the shipped value. For example:

# my-printer.cfg

# Slower final approach into the docks
[creator5_toolchanger]
dock_approach_speed: 80

# A finer bed mesh
[bed_mesh]
probe_count: 9, 9

# Your own macro
[gcode_macro PARK_FRONT]
description: Park the toolhead at the front
gcode:
    G90
    G1 X130 Y10 F12000

A macro you define again here replaces the shipped one, since its gcode is just another option. To see which value Klipper actually used, open http://<printer-ip>:7125/printer/objects/query?configfile=settings in a browser, or check the config dump near the top of printer.log after a restart.

Leave calibration to SAVE_CONFIG

Don't put values that calibration saves, like input shaper, PID, the bed mesh or the probe z_offset, in your own file. SAVE_CONFIG refuses to save an option whose value comes from an included file. Run the calibration and let SAVE_CONFIG store the result at the bottom of printer.cfg.

Note

You can't remove a section from another file this way, only change its options. To turn a section off, comment it out where it is. Updates keep that edit like any other.

items.title: Editing the shipped files
items.text: Editing a template directly is fine too. Updates keep your change unless they change the same lines. It's the better choice for small fixes in place, like commenting out a line, where an override file can't help.

items.title: Resolving a conflict
items.text:
When an update and your edit changed the same lines, the updater leaves your file alone and writes <file>.conflict next to it. Your printer keeps running on your version; only that file's update is waiting. The updater's log is /tmp/opencreator-updater.log on the printer.

  1. Open <file>.conflict. Each conflict shows your version (current) and the update's (latest):

    <<<<<<< current
dock_approach_speed: 80
=======
dock_approach_speed: 100
>>>>>>> latest

  2. Keep the lines you want, delete the other side and the three marker lines.

  3. Copy the result over the original file, delete the .conflict file, and restart Klipper.

The next update merges from there. Moving your changes to your own file (above) stops them from conflicting again.

items.title: Going back
items.text:
• One option: delete it from your own file, or put the shipped value back.
  • A whole file: the last template the updater applied is kept in .opencreator-updater/base/<file>. Copy it over your file to get the shipped version back.
  • Everything: Restore backup in the OpenCreator Installer, if you made a backup when you installed.

Keep a copy of my-printer.cfg somewhere safe. It's all you need to set a fresh install up the way you like it.

items.title: Contributing documentation
items.text:
Edit pages under docs/ and add new pages to nav in mkdocs.yml. For hardware instructions, say which printer model, firmware version and source commit they're for, and how they were tested. Say plainly when something hasn't been tested.

Make sure to use clear language and only delve into techincal specs and docs on parts where it would be expected.

Before proposing a change, build the site with warnings treated as errors:

.venv/bin/python -m zensical build --strict

On Windows, use .venv\Scripts\python.exe. The generated site/ directory is ignored by Git; only the source Markdown and configuration should be committed.

items.title: Videos and other raw HTML
items.text: Markdown images and links work with relative paths. Paths inside raw HTML, such as <video> or <source src="...">, don't: the site loads pages without a full reload, and a relative src is then resolved against the page you came from. Give media in raw HTML its full URL, for example https://opencreatorcfw.github.io/assets/videos/<file>.mp4.

items.title: The difference with OpenCreator
items.text:
There's a plethora of mods now for the Creator 5, what makes us different?

It's not special that there's a couple mods apart from us now. Even though we were first on the scene with our stock mods, doesn't mean we stopped innovating when others came out with their solutions.

items.title: Features
items.text:
We're the first to fully reverse all MCU code and thus, can improve certain features with it such as allowing for double stepping on the extruder motor, having completely addressable TMC2209s instead of hardcoding. Due to it no longer being hardcoded, you can now adjust motor current on the fly for the extruder.

This also makes our firmware completely incompatible with stock and other mods that piggy back off of the stock firmware which is all at the time of writing.

We're also currently the only custom firmware that has this.

We also actively take in suggestions.

We also have Power Loss Recovery, which isn't a given as most CFWs made do not have fully implemented PLR. On power loss, it will prompt you to restart your print, and will keep the bed warmed, so even if you aren't there, your print can be saved.

items.title: Up to 2x faster toolchanges
items.text:
A stock toolchange usually takes about 6 seconds. On OpenCreator CFW one can take as little as 3 seconds, so multi-color and multi-material prints spend far less time swapping tools.

Watch the toolchange video

items.title: Better timelapses
items.text:
OpenCreator CFW takes a camera frame at every layer change and turns them into a smooth MP4 when the print finishes, using Moonraker Timelapse. The videos are under Timelapse in Fluidd and Mainsail, where you can also change the frame rate or park the toolhead for each frame.

Watch the timelapse

items.title: Fixes stock firmware bugs
items.text: FlashForge's firmware has a bug where switching extruders whilst one is unloading can make the extruder run backwards. OpenCreator CFW fixes this.

items.title: Klipper
items.text: We're fully Kalico, a fork of Klipper with more features. No FlashForge, no old Klipper.

items.title: Different hosts
items.text: You're not forced to cope with a bad SoC with the printer, just plug in a new host like a Raspberry Pi, and get to printing!

items.title: Support over Discord
items.text: Unlike others, we have a centralized Discord where we take feedback and support people. Check it out on the landing page.

items.title: Support for stock installs
items.text: If you really don't want to break too much of your warranty, you can stick with OpenCreator Legacy, where we only modify a little bit, and keep things mostly stock, FlashForge services and all.

items.title: Maintainable Source
items.text: Unlike some other mods, our source code is easily readable and is reasonably split up on the repository, making it very easy to understand what we do.

items.title: Mainstream UIs
items.text: Most of our UIs and backends such as Mainsail and Fluidd, along with Moonraker are mainstream, not forked, and only come with a CSS theme, update as soon as updates come out.

items.title: Up to 3x* better performance
items.text:
With our custom compiled special ingredients that we sprinkle into our custom firmware, you are less likely to ever run into a Timer Too Close, or Motor Too Far In The Past, and can run a print without a purge tower without the printer crashing.

(* - 3x best case scenario, most of the time from 1.5 to 2x from completely stock 1.9.9)

items.title: No slowed-down short moves
items.text:
Since 1.9.9, stock firmware avoids Timer Too Close by slowing down short moves, whether your print needed it or not:

  • Every move of 0.75 mm or less is slowed so it takes at least 2.5 ms. A 0.2 mm move can go no faster than 80 mm/s, however fast the slicer asked for.
  • Any short move that extrudes (0.75 mm or less across) is capped at 80 mm/s.
  • On top of that, the motion planner limits acceleration on them. In 1.9.9, always: short moves to 5000 mm/s², and short extruding moves to 80 mm/s at 1500 mm/s². In 2.0.0, moves of 0.3 mm or less are limited to 10000 mm/s², and extruding moves of 0.5 mm or less to 120 mm/s at 5000 mm/s². That applies when moves come in faster than 80 a second (fully from 200), and for the first 100 moves of a print.

Curves, arcs, small details and fine infill are made of exactly these short moves, so stock prints them slower than the slicer planned for.

OpenCreator CFW has none of these limits: every move runs at the speed in your G-code. We keep up with the moves instead of slowing them down (see above).

items.title: Full installer
items.text: Instead of picking afterwards, or not being able to pick at all, our installer environment will allow you to pick what you like, before it even installs, and if your printer breaks but can still access USB drives, you can use our installer to fix any problems, over SSH.

items.title: Better VFA compensation
items.text:
FlashForge keeps a lot of their special sauce for their VFA calibration disabled. We fix up their disabled options and make it better.

Read the wiki page on VFA Compensation

items.title: Early boot and recovery stick
items.text: FlashForge updates overwrite /usr/prog/app_startup.sh and firmwareExe, the two files that normally start OpenCreator. So OpenCreator also boots from a file their updates don't overwrite: /usr/prog/module/driver.sh. Stock's rootfs runs it at every boot, long before app_startup.sh. The same file runs a recovery script from a USB stick, so a printer whose startup is broken can still be fixed without opening it up.

items.title: Safer than stock
items.text:
On a stock printer the only way to recover without opening it up is a FlashForge update on a USB stick. That check lives in app_startup.sh, the same script mods edit and FlashForge updates overwrite. If that script breaks (a bad edit, a mod, a write cut off by a power loss), the USB check goes with it, and the printer needs Ingenic USB boot, which means opening the electronics bay.

What breaks Stock OpenCreator app_startup.sh (bad edit, mod, half-written) no USB recovery, no Wi-Fi; open the printer driver.sh still boots OpenCreator with Wi-Fi and SSH, and still runs runRecovery.sh from a stick a FlashForge update replaces app_startup.sh and firmwareExe n/a driver.sh isn't touched; stock boots, as you asked for OpenCreator's firmwareExe is deleted n/a driver.sh leaves it to app_startup.sh, which puts FlashForge's firmwareExe back (stock screen and Wi-Fi) driver.sh itself is broken n/a stock's S11 just carries on; app_startup.sh boots OpenCreator the old way

Other details that help:

  • driver.sh is started by stock's rootfs, which is read-only while the printer runs, so mods can't change that. A FlashForge update can ship a new rootfs (squashfs); one that drops the driver.sh call is unlikely, but then OpenCreator boots the old way through app_startup.sh.
  • driver.sh and firmwareExe are written to a temporary file first and renamed into place, so a power loss never leaves half a file.
  • A boot lock makes sure OpenCreator starts once, whichever of driver.sh and app_startup.sh gets there first.
  • Klipper and the rest only start once Wi-Fi has an address (or after 15 s), so SSH is there when you need it.

items.title: Boot order
items.text:
flowchart TD
    A["rcS (read-only rootfs)"] --> B["S09: mount /usr/prog"]
    B --> C["S11: /usr/prog/module/driver.sh"]
    C --> D["mount /usr/data"]
    D --> E{"USB stick with runRecovery.sh?"}
    E -- yes --> F["run it, log to the stick"]
    E -- no --> G
    F --> G["start OpenCreator in the background"]
    C --> H["S21..S50: /usr/data, network, SSH"]
    H --> I["S99: app_startup.sh"]
    I --> J["firmwareExe: already started, stays alive"]

driver.sh starts OpenCreator once app_startup.sh has set up /etc (or after 60 s if it never does). It loads the Wi-Fi, touch and coprocessor modules first, the same ones app_startup.sh loads. When app_startup.sh later starts firmwareExe, that copy sees OpenCreator is already running and only stays alive. If app_startup.sh is broken, or a FlashForge update replaced it, OpenCreator still boots.

driver.sh leaves the boot to app_startup.sh when:

Condition Why firmwareExe is FlashForge's original program stock was flashed or you rolled back a FlashForge update (Creator5*.tgz or runFirmwareExe.sh) is on a USB stick stock flashes it first a control-board update is pending stock updates the boards first firmwareExe is an older OpenCreator one without the boot lock it would start OpenCreator twice

Before starting Klipper and the rest, firmwareExe waits until Wi-Fi has an address, at most 15 s. Without one it starts anyway, and keeps trying Wi-Fi in the background.

items.title: Recovery stick
items.text:
Put a runRecovery.sh in the root of a USB stick (FAT32, exFAT or ext4), plug it in and power the printer on. driver.sh runs it as root at every boot while the stick is in:

  • before network, SSH and app_startup.sh, and even if /usr/data won't mount;
  • from the stick's folder, with $RECOVERY_DIR set to it, so it can use files next to it;
  • its output is added to runRecovery.log on the stick.

OpenCreator then boots as usual. Take the stick out when you're done, or make the script safe to run twice.

A script that saves the boot logs to the stick:

#!/bin/sh
OUT="$RECOVERY_DIR/recovery-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
dmesg > "$OUT/dmesg.txt"
cp /tmp/*.log "$OUT/" 2>/dev/null
cp /usr/prog/app_startup.sh* "$OUT/" 2>/dev/null
tail -n 2000 /usr/data/opencreator/klipper/logs/printer.log > "$OUT/printer.log" 2>/dev/null
sync

Warning

The script runs as root with nothing in its way. Only use scripts you trust, and keep in mind that anyone with physical access can do the same.

FlashForge .tgz updates on a stick still install through stock's app_startup.sh as before.

items.title: Files
items.text:
File on the printer What Installed by /usr/prog/module/driver.sh the early boot hook stock runs at S11 the installer, then the updater from opencreator-fs firmware/driver.sh; removed again by a rollback to stock /usr/prog/PROGRAM/software/firmwareExe OpenCreator's launcher (Wi-Fi, then the startup scripts) the installer and the updater /usr/data/opencreator/firmware/ the copies of both they install from the installer and the updater Log What /tmp/early.log driver.sh: USB stick, and whether it started OpenCreator /tmp/opencreator.log firmwareExe and the startup scripts runRecovery.log (on the stick) the recovery script's output

Technical details: CREATOR5_EARLY_BOOT.md in opencreator-fs.

items.title: Games on the Creator 5
items.text:
The Creator 5 runs on an Ingenic X2600, a low-power embedded chip that's very slow by modern standards. That's what makes these ports a feat: real games running on hardware that was never meant to do much more than drive a print UI.

These are community-built ports you can install on OpenCreator CFW.

Games are not part of printing

Games run on the printer's application processor, separate from the motion firmware. They don't affect printing, but don't run them while a print is in progress. The touchscreen will be used as the display and actively shares resources.

items.title: DOOM
items.text:
The classic 1993 shooter, running on the Creator 5's touchscreen with on-screen controls (D-pad, action buttons, and the status bar).

DOOM is driven by the open WAD asset files, so you can also load custom levels and total conversions.

items.title: DOOM WADs
items.text:
DOOM's game data lives in .wad files. The engine is free; you supply a WAD:

  • Registered DOOM.WAD / DOOM2.WAD - from a retail copy you own.
  • Community WADs - free fan-made levels and total conversions (many are standalone and need no retail files, includes FreeDOOM).

Drop the WAD onto the printer and point the port at it. Touch controls work the same as the stock episode.

items.title: Sonic Mania
items.text: Sonic Mania, the 2017 & 2018 platformer by SEGA, Christian Whitehead, PagodaWest Games and Headcannon, running at full speed during 2D sections, and almost full speed during 3D sections to get emeralds. Fully completable from start to finish. Using RSDK 5U.

items.title: Installing
items.text: Games are installed as git repositories. Some may not be available, and need to be asked for.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• These are made by OpenCreator, but not encouraged. Expect rough edges.
  • Touch input is mapped to on-screen buttons, and some games may support gamepad input or keyboard.
  • Performance is limited by the slow embedded processor, and may encounter slowdown.

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
OpenCreator has two paths. Legacy keeps the mostly stock FlashForge control stack and adds selected modifications. OpenCreator CFW replaces more of that stack with community-maintained Klipper and printer-side components. CFW is in public alpha: download the latest release and see Installation and safety.

If you want to improve a stock printer today, start with the Creator-5-Mods Legacy guides. Follow the prerequisites for each individual modification.

If you are contributing to CFW, start with Project layout and Architecture. The printer configuration lives in opencreator-fs/fs/usr/data/config, while the Creator 5 Klipper modules and MCU code live in kalico. The detailed toolchanger development notes are in CREATOR5_TOOLCHANGER.md inside the configuration tree.

Join our Discord for support and to report problems with the alpha.

items.title: Before installing on a printer
items.text:
• Read Status and roadmap
  • Read Installation and safety
  • Know how to revert to stock firmware
  • Have a USB drive that meets the requirements
  • Join the Discord for support

items.title: Installation and safety
items.text:
OpenCreator CFW is in public alpha. Download the latest release on GitHub.

Alpha

This is an alpha. Expect bugs, keep a backup, and know how to go back to stock. Report problems on the Discord.

CFW is installed with the OpenCreator Installer, a touchscreen app that backs up the printer before changing anything. If you want a mostly stock printer instead, use the Legacy path and its own instructions.

items.title: Supported FlashForge firmware
items.text:
OpenCreator supports every FlashForge firmware version released for the Creator 5 and Creator 5 Pro, from 1.7.8 up to the latest, 2.0.0. You don't need to update or downgrade before installing.

FlashForge firmware Kernel package 1.7.8 to 1.9.7 2.0.1 to 2.0.5 1.9.8 2.0.6 1.9.9 2.0.7 2.0.0 2.0.8

A newer FlashForge release with a new kernel needs an installer update first; until then the installer stops without changing anything. See Supported kernel packages.

items.title: Requirements for USB
items.text:
• FAT32 Partition
  • At least 4GB in size
  • USB is recommended to have at least 8GB for the backup step

items.title: Requirement for printer
items.text:
• A printer that has at least 200MB on the prog partition and 1gb of storage on the data partition
  • A printer that has an active and stable internet connection of at least 1 mbps

items.title: Steps to install OpenCreator
items.text:
1. Download the zip from the latest release and extract it to the root of the USB drive.
  2. Reboot the printer with the USB drive plugged in.
  3. Follow the on-screen steps. If you're not sure what "tunneled" means, choose a SoC install.
  4. Wait about 15-30 minutes for the install (backing up takes the longest).
  5. When it finishes, you'll be prompted to remove the USB drive and press reboot.
  6. After rebooting you'll see the new boot logo and GrumpyScreen on the touchscreen, and Fluidd in your browser at the printer's IP.
  7. Set up your slicer for OpenCreator: follow Slicer Configuration before your first print.

items.title: Steps to update OpenCreator
items.text: There are two ways.

items.title: Way 1: Fluidd/Mainsail
items.text:
Fluidd and Mainsail have a way for smaller updates that don't affect most packages on the printer.

  1. Navigate to the software update section
  2. Update "OpenCreator" then "Klipper"
  3. Reboot via switch or host restart

items.title: Way 2: OpenCreator Installer Update
items.text:
Sometimes an update can't be distributed like that, this is the other way for more major updates.

  1. Load the update by copying files overtop the existing files
  2. Plug in the USB drive and reboot
  3. Update with backups or without backups (Backups will make it last significantly longer and are not required for updates)
  4. Restart when it prompts you

items.title: Uninstalling OpenCreator
items.text:
To uninstall OpenCreator and go back to bone stock, launch the installer, and follow instructions for a full rollback

Files left over

Some files are left over after uninstalling. They can be removed manually: /usr/data/opencreator, /usr/data/grumpyscreen, and /usr/data/python-hf.

Moonraker is also updated by OpenCreator, so if you go back to stock you'll need to reinstall FlashForge's original version from their download.

If you picked Fluidd during install, you'll also need to revert Nginx to the stock config.

The SSH login banner doesn't need cleaning up: a rollback removes it, and it turns itself off whenever FlashForge's firmware is back in place.

items.title: Restoring the stock boot logo
items.text:
The OpenCreator boot logo will be removed when you use the full-rollback option. Here's a way if you do it via normal software updates.

  1. Download the stock logo
  2. Copy it over /usr/prog/logo.jpeg on the printer, keeping that file name
  3. Reboot the printer

items.title: OpenCreator Installer
items.text: The OpenCreator Installer is a touchscreen app that runs on the Creator 5's own screen. It walks you through installing OpenCreator CFW from a USB drive: on the printer itself, or tunneled to a Raspberry Pi / SBC. It backs everything up first, so you can go back. Its source is the opencreator-installer repository.

items.title: Download
items.text: The installer is part of each OpenCreator release; use the latest one. Extract the zip to the root of a FAT32 USB drive, then follow Steps to install OpenCreator.

items.title: What you need
items.text:
• A Creator 5 or Creator 5 Pro on FlashForge firmware (1.9.9 recommended)
  • A USB drive that meets the requirements
  • Internet on the printer (Entware, Kalico, Moonraker and the web UIs are downloaded during install)
  • For tunnel mode: an SBC, see OpenCreator for SBC
  • A printer that has at least 200MB on the prog partition and 1gb of storage on the data partition

items.title: How it goes
items.text:
flowchart TD
  A[Check printer model<br/>and kernel package] --> B{Supported?}
  B -->|no| S[Stop: nothing is changed]
  B -->|yes| E{Where should<br/>Klipper run?}
  E -->|On printer SoC| F[Choose Fluidd or Mainsail]
  F --> G[Install GrumpyScreen?]
  E -->|Tunneled| G
  G --> H[Ready to install:<br/>summary]
  H --> I[Back up, then install]
  I --> J[Reboot]
  1. Checking. The installer reads the printer model and FlashForge kernel package. The printer's root filesystem is not changed; everything is installed next to the stock software. The bottom of the screen shows the installer version, the MCU firmware on the drive (and what the boards last got, if OpenCreator flashed them before), the kernel package and the build date.

2. Where should Klipper run? On printer SoC installs everything on the printer. Tunneled turns the printer's board into a bridge for an SBC. Both work on every supported FlashForge firmware version. Choosing Tunneled asks for the tunneled-mode password, typed on the screen's keyboard, both for a first install and for switching an installed printer to tunneled. It isn't asked again when the printer is already tunneled.

3. Web interface (SoC only): Fluidd (recommended) or Mainsail. Both are installed; the one you pick is the one the printer's web page shows.

4. Touchscreen: install GrumpyScreen (recommended) or not.

5. Ready to install shows the printer, mode, web UI and touchscreen you chose. Back up and install starts; Install without backup skips the backup (faster when re-running); Demo install does a dry run (below).

6. Installing shows each step live with its number (Step 3 of 11), a progress bar and elapsed time. Installing Entware and the Python packages takes a while.

7. Installation complete: reboot from the button, then unplug the USB drive.

items.title: Already installed
items.text:
If the printer already has OpenCreator from the same installer version, the installer opens on OpenCreator is up to date:

  • Update again re-runs the update with the current setup.
  • Recovery runs the whole setup again, as above.
  • Update Configs asks the same questions (where Klipper runs, web UI, touchscreen), then shows only what differs from the current setup and changes just that. For example, switching from On printer SoC to Tunneled only installs the bridge, and switching back only installs what SoC mode needs and isn't on the printer yet. Switching web UI changes which one the printer serves; turning the touchscreen off keeps GrumpyScreen on the printer but stops starting it. Nothing is backed up. Reboot afterwards.
  • Restore backup and Rollback to stock show up when there's a backup or FlashForge's own firmwareExe to go back to.

items.title: Update available
items.text: With an older OpenCreator installed, it opens on Update available, which updates in place with the setup shown. Your configs and files are kept; OpenCreator files you changed are saved to the backup. Change setup asks the questions again.

items.title: No internet
items.text: Without internet, it lists the Wi-Fi networks it can see. Tap one and type its password on the screen's keyboard. Quit starts the printer normally.

items.title: Clean up storage
items.text:
Every start page (first install, update, already installed, no internet, unsupported kernel) has Clean up storage. Its confirmation page warns that nothing can be brought back, and Yes, delete only works after a 10-second countdown. It deletes:

  • every print file (.gcode, .3mf, .stl), .mp4 and log under /usr/data and /usr/prog;
  • everything in /usr/data/logs, /usr/data/update (FlashForge update downloads), /usr/data/opencreator/timelapse, /usr/data/opencreator/klipper/logs and the Entware caches;
  • other mods' leftovers (ZMOD, Anvil), old Moonraker copies, and the stock Klipper docs and man pages.

Git checkouts (Klipper, Moonraker, opencreator-fs and the rest), the stock firmware's own model files and the installer's backups are kept. It can't be undone, and OpenCreator takes no responsibility for anything it breaks or removes. Based on CleanFlashforgeCreator5Pro.

Supported kernel packages

Entware needs legacy NaN, which is switched on with one byte written at an address that depends on the FlashForge kernel package (/usr/prog/PROGRAM/kernel/): 0x00a130d1 for 2.0.1 to 2.0.6, 0x00B330D1 for 2.0.7 (FlashForge 1.9.9) and 0x00B030D1 for 2.0.8 (FlashForge 2.0.0). On any other package the installer stops without changing anything.

items.title: What gets installed
items.text: On printer SoCTunneled Step What happens Entware The Entware package manager in /usr/data/bin/opt, with git, gcc, Python and Moonraker's build dependencies. LoopScript OpenCreator's startup system from opencreator-fs: it replaces FlashForge's firmwareExe (a copy of the original is kept) and starts everything below at boot. It also installs the early boot hook (/usr/prog/module/driver.sh), which boots OpenCreator even if app_startup.sh breaks and runs a recovery script from a USB stick, and replaces the boot logo with the OpenCreator one (the original is backed up). A rollback to stock removes the hook. MCU firmware Flashes all four boards (eBoard, heaterBoard, levelBoard, mainBoardGD) from the package on the USB drive, after checking its checksum. Skipped if the boards already run that firmware. Klipper Kalico with the OpenCreator printer config, including the first-time setup dialog and the OpenCreator Fluidd theme, in /usr/data/opencreator/klipper. A first install takes the printer's input shaper and hotend and bed PID tuning from FlashForge's config; a config you already have there is kept. Moonraker The latest Moonraker, replacing FlashForge's older one. Its update manager lists Kalico, Moonraker, Mainsail, Fluidd and opencreator (the OpenCreator configs). Updating opencreator merges the new config templates into yours within a minute, keeping your own edits. Restart Klipper afterwards to load them. Web UI The latest Mainsail and Fluidd; the printer's web page shows the one you chose. Touchscreen The latest GrumpyScreen release, if chosen. Root login Adds the root login opencreator (password FlashForge2026) for SSH. See Root login. Step What happens Entware The Entware package manager, with git, gcc and socat. LoopScript Same as SoC mode; in tunnel mode it starts the bridge instead of Klipper. MCU firmware Same as SoC mode. Bridge Installs the socat bridge and switches the printer's board to bridge-only mode, so it forwards the four boards to your SBC over USB. Touchscreen The latest GrumpyScreen release, if chosen. Point it at your SBC afterwards: set host under [moonraker] in /usr/data/grumpyscreen/grumpyscreen.cfg. Root login Same as SoC mode. SBC Not done by the installer: after rebooting the printer, run the SBC installer from OpenCreator for SBC.

items.title: Root login
items.text:
The installer adds a root login, so you can SSH into the printer:

User opencreator Password FlashForge2026 
ssh opencreator@<printer IP>

Change the password

Everyone who installs OpenCreator gets the same default password. To set your own, log in over SSH and run:

passwd opencreator

Type the new password twice. Running the installer again keeps the password you set.

items.title: Login banner
items.text:
Logging in over SSH shows the OpenCreator logo next to some details about the printer, with the model underneath:

    ▗▟████████████▙▞▜███████████▄       OpenCreator

  ▐██▌            ███▌                  Uptime   2d 13h 22m
  ▐██▌            ███▌                  IP       192.168.2.92 (wlan0)
  ▐██▌            ███▌                  Storage  1.8 GB free of 5.5 GB in /usr/data
  ▐██▙▖           ▜██▙        ▄▄▄▄▖     Host     flashforge
